newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa industrials hit new highs, golds slip.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa industrials hit new highs, golds slip.

text.p: South African industrial shares raced through the 9,000 point barrier for the first time on Wednesday as positive comment from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan sent global markets soaring.

On Tuesday, Greenspan gave an upbeat analysis of the U.S. economy, sending New York shares higher overnight. South African stocks responded by also heading upwards, though most trade was in second-line stocks, not major blue-chips.
The industrials index pushed up 47.4 points to a new closing high of 9,032.3 as the all-share index added 16.7 points to 7,446.9.
Dealers said the market, which has recently been ignoring trends on Wall Street, was set to watch the U.S. bourse again for direction on Thursday.
Total volumes were healthy with more than 1.3 billion rands worth of shares changing hands, but gold shares sickened slightly as bullion seemed stuck around $324 an ounce.
The golds index dropped 10.8 points to 982.4, but dealers said the losses were not seen as too worrying just yet after recent gains.
